record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: For the regime mπ/2 < µ < mN/3 at low temperature, how do complex phase cancellations operate so that physically the quark-number expectation value can remain zero even though individual gauge configurations can already give nonzero quark number? Equivalently, what is the detailed phase-distribution mechanism that enforces the Silver-Blaze behavior in this interval?

Of course, the latter is merely a conjecture and we do not know how this can happen.
It is not known how the phase is distributed at µ = mπ/2 in QCD and whether the expectation value of the quark number becomes zero.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice QCD with $N_f$ light quark flavors at nonzero baryon chemical potential $\mu$ and low temperature $T \to 0$. Let $m_\pi$ denote the pion mass and $m_N$ the nucleon mass. The grand-canonical partition function is

$$Z(\mu) = \int \mathcal{D}U\, e^{-S_g[U]}\, \det M(U,\mu),$$

where $S_g[U]$ is the gauge action and $M(U,\mu)$ is the quark Dirac operator on a gauge background $U$. For $\mu \neq 0$, $\det M(U,\mu)$ is in general complex; write $\det M(U,\mu) = |\det M(U,\mu)|\, e^{i\theta(U,\mu)}$. The expectation value of the quark number operator $\hat{n}$ on a single gauge configuration is generally nonzero, $\hat{n}[U,\mu] \neq 0$, yet the Silver-Blaze property requires that the full ensemble expectation value $\langle \hat{n}\rangle$ vanish for $\mu$ below the physical onset $\mu < m_N/3$.

In the interval $m_\pi/2 < \mu < m_N/3$, where the phase-quenched theory has already undergone pion condensation but full QCD has not yet reached baryon onset, determine the precise mechanism by which the distribution of the phase $\theta(U,\mu)$ over the gauge ensemble produces cancellations that enforce

$$\langle \hat{n}\rangle = \frac{1}{Z(\mu)}\int \mathcal{D}U\, e^{-S_g[U]}\, \det M(U,\mu)\, \hat{n}[U,\mu] = 0.$$

Specifically, characterize the joint distribution of $\theta(U,\mu)$ and $\hat{n}[U,\mu]$ on configurations weighted by $e^{-S_g[U]}|\det M(U,\mu)|$ that is responsible for the exact cancellation of the quark-number contributions, and show how this distribution evolves with $\mu$ across the interval $(m_\pi/2,\, m_N/3)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and lattice studies (including a 2026 review on the Silver Blaze problem in QCD and complex Langevin equation-of-state work in 2022) indicate that, while the Silver Blaze phenomenon is widely observed and discussed, the detailed mechanism by which phase cancellations enforce vanishing quark number in the interval m_π/2 < μ < m_N/3 remains unresolved. The mechanism leading to such cancellations is described in the literature as still unknown.

status_evidence.title: The Silver Blaze Problem in QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Review of the Silver Blaze problem stating that the cancellation mechanism via phase fluctuations of the fermion determinant remains an open issue.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanism enforcing Silver Blaze via phase cancellations in QCD is still considered an open problem.

status_evidence.title: QCD equation of state via the complex Langevin method
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice study using complex Langevin to probe finite-density QCD; reports observation of Silver Blaze behavior but does not resolve the analytic phase-distribution mechanism.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical lattice work observes Silver Blaze but does not provide a closed-form characterization of the phase distribution in the relevant μ window.
